name: Snake's head fritillary
grown_as: The wild species, grown by William both in a bed and by the pond. Drawn in its usual chequered purple form; about one plant in ten is white.
habit: Slender, upright single stems 15 to 40 cm tall with a few narrow leaves up them and one hanging bell at the top. Grassy and easily lost among grass until it flowers.

leaf.arrangement: Three to six leaves, alternate and spaced up the stem (not in a basal rosette)
leaf.outline: 6 to 12 cm long by 3 to 8 mm wide, tapering gradually to the tip
leaf.surface: Smooth, channelled, with a grey waxy bloom

flower.form: A large square-shouldered hanging bell, like a little lantern
flower.petals: Six tepals, free, oblong, held together in a bell that is wide at the top (squarish shoulders) and slightly narrower at the mouth
flower.colour: Chequered: a regular pattern of dark maroon-purple squares on a paler pinkish-lilac ground, like a chessboard. White form: white with faint green chequers.
flower.centre: Hidden inside: six yellow anthers and a three-branched style. A green nectar groove at the base of each tepal inside.
flower.carried: Usually one (sometimes two) per stem, hanging from the arching tip of the stem

fruit: The stem straightens and the capsule stands upright: oblong, three-sided with rounded angles, about 2 cm, green turning straw, splitting at the top to shake out flat brown seeds.
seedling: Not drawn. A single grass-like leaf; three to four years to flower.
winter: Nothing above ground until shoots appear in March.

palette_wish.flower: dull maroon-purple, about #6E2F55, with the paler squares pink-lilac

leaf: a narrow grass-like leaf tapering to a point
bloom: a hanging bell with square shoulders
a chequerboard of dark purple squares on a paler pink-lilac ground
bulb: a small bulb 1 to 2 cm of two or three fleshy white scales
shoots: a thin grey-green stem with narrow leaves on it, like grass
a single bud hanging at the tip
flower: a slender stem with a few narrow leaves spaced up it
one chequered bell hanging from the top
the bell large for the thin stem
seedhead: an upright oblong pod on a straightened stem

look_alikes: Nothing else in the UK has the chequered bell. Before flowering it looks like grass or a young bluebell, but its leaves are on the stem, not from the base. Other fritillaries (F. uva-vulpis, F. michailovskyi) are smaller, with unchequered bells.
